newsitem.title: UK: UK'S Imperial Tobacco buys Rizla.
newsitem.headline: UK'S Imperial Tobacco buys Rizla.

text.p: Imperial Tobacco Group Plc said on Tuesday that it had acquired Rizla International BV, the world's largest maker and seller of handrolling tobacco papers, for 168 million pounds ($272.7 million).
It said it would also acquire Rizla's outstanding debt of 17 million pounds, bringing the total investment in the Netherlands-based company to 185 million pounds.
Rizla, founded in 1796, is one of the oldest companies in the tobacco industry and has around 66 percent of the world market for branded handrolling tobacco papers, Imperial said.

Based in Breda, the Netherlands, Rizla has production facilities in Belgium, Wales and France. It made trading profit of 23 million pounds in 1996 on sales of 74 million and had net assets of some 17 million pounds at the year end.

"Rizla's extensive worldwide sales and distribution network will extend Imperial's international presence and provide significant opportunities for further expansion in international markets," Imperial chief executive Gareth Davis said in a statement.

"We are confident that Rizla will create substantial value for shareholders," he said. The company will be managed as a separate division, and Imperial said Rizla's existing senior management would remain in place. ($1=.6161 Pound)
